findings.fix: Add visible helper text under the password field (e.g. "At least 8 characters") in addition to the minlength attribute.
findings.violation: The password's minimum length requirement is encoded only as an HTML attribute; there is no visible hint telling the user the password must be at least 8 characters, so they only discover it after a failed submission.

findings.evidence: Address fields present are only "Street address" and "Postal code"
findings.fix: Add city and state/region inputs (e.g. with autocomplete="address-level2" and "address-level1") between street address and postal code.
findings.location: row-street and row-postal (`<input id="street-input" ... name="street_address">` ... `<input id="postal-input" ... name="postal_code">`)
findings.violation: The address section has no city and state/region fields, so a shipping address cannot actually be captured in full.

findings.evidence: `autocomplete="tel"` is identical to the primary phone field's `autocomplete="tel"`
findings.fix: Differentiate the fields, e.g. drop autocomplete on the secondary field or use a distinguishing value so autofill doesn't duplicate the primary number into it.
findings.violation: Using the same autocomplete token for both phone fields can cause browsers to autofill both inputs with the same number, defeating the purpose of a separate "secondary phone" field.

findings.evidence: `required=""` on a "Company website" field during personal account creation
findings.fix: Make this field optional, or remove it if it isn't actually needed for a personal retail account.
findings.location: row-website (`<label id="website-label" for="website-input">Company website</label> <input id="website-input" name="website" type="url" required="">`)
findings.violation: Requiring a company website to create what otherwise looks like a consumer shopping account (name, personal address, phone) will block individual customers who have no company or website.

findings.fix: Either add a pattern that accepts bare domains, or show inline guidance/example text indicating the "https://" prefix is required.
findings.violation: type="url" requires a fully qualified URI with scheme (e.g. "https://example.com"); users who type a bare domain like "example.com" will fail native validation with no explanation.

findings.evidence: `placeholder="Must be 8 digits"` with no `pattern` or `maxlength` attribute
findings.fix: Add `pattern="\d{8}"` and `maxlength="8"`, and move the "Must be 8 digits" instruction into persistent helper text rather than the placeholder.
findings.location: row-member (`<input id="member-input" ... placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">`)
findings.violation: The 8-digit requirement is conveyed only through placeholder text, which disappears once the user starts typing, and there is no pattern/maxlength to actually enforce 8 digits.

findings.evidence: No description accompanies "Account number", immediately following "Membership number (8 digits)"
findings.fix: Add explanatory text clarifying what this account number is and where to find it, or remove the field if it duplicates membership number.
findings.violation: It's unclear what distinguishes "Account number" from "Membership number" - the field appears redundant or under-explained, risking user confusion about which number to enter.

findings.evidence: Both "Overnight" and "Next-day" appear as separate options in the same select
findings.fix: Merge these into a single clearly-labeled option (e.g. "Overnight / Next-day") or differentiate them with explicit delivery-time details.
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" shipping are generally the same thing, so offering both as distinct choices is confusing and ambiguous for the user.

findings.evidence: `autocomplete="name"` duplicates the value already used on `name-input` ("Full name") earlier in the form
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate "legal_name" field, or clearly differentiate its purpose from "Full name" (e.g. label it "Legal name (if different from full name)") and give it a distinct autocomplete value.
findings.location: row-legalname (`<label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label> <input id="legalname-input" name="legal_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" ... required="">`)
findings.violation: Two separate required fields ("Full name" and "Your name") both collect a person's name and share the same autocomplete token, which is redundant for the user and will cause browsers to autofill both identically despite them appearing to request different information.

findings.evidence: No `autocomplete` attribute present; `style="font-size:16px"` applied only here
findings.fix: Add `autocomplete="organization"`, and either apply the same font-size rule to all text inputs via a shared stylesheet rule or remove the one-off inline style.
findings.location: row-org (`<input id="org-input" name="organization" type="text" style="font-size:16px" required="">`)
findings.violation: The field is missing `autocomplete="organization"`, and the inline `font-size:16px` (likely intended to prevent mobile zoom-on-focus) is applied inconsistently - only to this input and not to the other text inputs (name, email, password, street, etc.), so mobile zoom behavior will differ field to field.

findings.evidence: `type="text"` with no format hint, and a one-off `style="display:block"` on this label not used on any other label
findings.fix: Use a structured control (e.g. type="time" or a select of time ranges) and move any shared label styling into CSS applied uniformly to all labels.
findings.location: row-contacttime (`<label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:block">Preferred contact time</label> <input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required="">`)
findings.violation: A free-text input for "contact time" with no structure or example will produce inconsistent, hard-to-parse values (e.g. "morning" vs "9am" vs "9:00-12:00"), and the inline display:block style is applied inconsistently compared to other labels in the form.

findings.evidence: Button has `type="button"` with no associated script, handler, or explanation visible in the document
findings.fix: Either wire it to an actual action (e.g. toggling an order/plan summary) or remove it from the form.
findings.violation: "View details" appears to be a non-functional/dead button sitting right before the submit button, which is confusing since it has no defined behavior.
